name: Citron Pound Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of citron
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of citron

instructions.text: Stir two cups of butter to a cream.
Beat in the following ingredients each one in succession: one pint of powdered sugar, one quart of flour, a teaspoonful of salt.
Beat the yolks and whites of eight eggs separately and add them.
Then last of all add a quarter of a pound of citron cut into thin slices and floured.
Line two cake pans with buttered paper and turn the cake batter in.
Bake in a moderate oven about three-quarters of an hour.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stir two cups of butter to a cream.
2. Beat in the following ingredients each one in succession: one pint of powdered sugar, one quart of flour, a teaspoonful of salt.
3. Beat the yolks and whites of eight eggs separately and add them.
4. Add a wine-glass of brandy.
5. Then last of all add a quarter of a pound of citron cut into thin slices and floured.
6. Line two cake pans with buttered paper and turn the cake batter in.
7. Bake in a moderate oven about three-quarters of an hour.
